title: The cards, again
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The index cards, a third year. THANKFUL FOR. Wood brings them to the shack this time, not the newsroom. GULLIVER: maple bars, again. FINCH: writes something and turns it face down. STERLING: the card blank; she isn't here to leave it blank herself. The uncle takes a card nobody offered him.

panels.composition: The shack's counter — rule four be damned — three index cards and a pen. GULLY writing. WOOD. The UNCLE in the chair in the door. BARNABY.

image.prompt: three index cards and a pen on a bait shack counter with a teenager writing on one, a young man beside him, an old man in a lawn chair in the doorway, black and white, no words
image.notes: Cards per objects.md: year three. Letter after: THANKFUL FOR — GULLIVER: maple bars.

panels.composition: GULLIVER's card: maple bars. FINCH's: written, turned face down. STERLING's: blank.

image.prompt: close on three index cards on a counter, one with a short answer, one face down, one blank, black and white, no words
image.notes: FINCH's answer: face down; reserved. STERLING's: blank, in her absence.

panels.composition: The uncle's hand taking a fourth card from the stack. Nobody offered. Writing. Slow.

image.prompt: close on an old man's hand taking an index card and writing on it slowly, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle's card set face down on top of Wood's. Two face down, one blank, one maple bars. The strip doesn't turn them. It never will.

image.prompt: four index cards on a counter, two face down, one blank and one written, an old man's hand withdrawing, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Year three. Two face down, one blank. The uncle's card: reserved forever.
